limitation: The vacancy-rate parameter is held at its published 2023 census value (5.39%; on the consistent definition 2023 is the series maximum, 5.38%, minimum 4.01% in 1996); the starting surplus and the 2026 overbuild raise implied stock vacancy temporarily and are absorbed by 2035, so implied vacancy returns to the parameter (5.39% in 2050). The 2026 overbuild (market excess ≈15,700 dwellings over 2026-2050, of which ≈14,100 in 2026-2028) is absorbed by 2035 along the normalised logistic of the levers (≈34,700 dwellings built less; implied vacancy peaks at 6.72% in 2028). Stock-flow theory of the housing market (Rosen & Smith 1983; Wheaton 1990; DiPasquale & Wheaton 1992; Gabriel & Nothaft 2001) fixes the direction, reversion of vacancy to its equilibrium rate, not the speed; 2035 is the common RECC adoption window of the model and the speed is bracketed by sensitivity rows (never absorbed, by 2030, by 2045). The persistence rho = 0.43 describes how the flow deviation fades, not the payback of the stock.
